# Captain Jim

## Overview

- **Age:** 76 years old in Volume 4  <sub>[v4 c7 P48](../source/v04-c07.md#nw-v04-c07-p0048)</sub>
- **Gender:** Male  <sub>[v4 c2 P21](../source/v04-c02.md#nw-v04-c02-p0021)</sub>
- **Status:** Deceased  <sub>[v4 c39 P28](../source/v04-c39.md#nw-v04-c39-p0028)</sub>
- **Origin:** Four Winds, Prince Edward Island  <sub>[v4 c7 P4](../source/v04-c07.md#nw-v04-c07-p0004), [v4 c7 P5](../source/v04-c07.md#nw-v04-c07-p0005)</sub>
- **Role:** Lighthouse keeper and former sea captain  <sub>[v4 c2 P22](../source/v04-c02.md#nw-v04-c02-p0022), [v4 c9 P3](../source/v04-c09.md#nw-v04-c09-p0003)</sub>
- **Titles:** Captain Jim  <sub>[v4 c6 P10](../source/v04-c06.md#nw-v04-c06-p0010)</sub>
- **Nicknames:** Captain Jim  <sub>[v4 c6 P10](../source/v04-c06.md#nw-v04-c06-p0010)</sub>

## Appearance

Captain Jim is a tall, stooped, and rather ungainly man with an exceptionally rugged, plain face. He has deeply lined, bronzed skin, a thick mane of iron-gray hair falling to his shoulders, and remarkably clear, deep-set blue eyes. His hands are sinewy and brown from a lifetime spent at sea.

_Sources: [v4 c6 P14](../source/v04-c06.md#nw-v04-c06-p0014), [v4 c6 P15](../source/v04-c06.md#nw-v04-c06-p0015), [v4 c18 P7](../source/v04-c18.md#nw-v04-c18-p0007), [v4 c35 P37](../source/v04-c35.md#nw-v04-c35-p0037)_

## Personality

Possessing a simple-minded, high-souled nature, Captain Jim is renowned for his endless store of sea yarns, genial humor, and deep inner wisdom. He is a passionate lover of beauty and a deeply reverent, spiritual man who views life with unshakeable optimism and patience. Known as the 'race that knows Joseph,' he possesses a rare capacity for deep, lifelong devotion, never forgetting a friend or a love. Though gentle and polite, he holds a fierce hatred for cruelty, particularly toward women and helpless animals.

_Sources: [v4 c6 P14](../source/v04-c06.md#nw-v04-c06-p0014), [v4 c7 P59](../source/v04-c07.md#nw-v04-c07-p0059), [v4 c9 P40](../source/v04-c09.md#nw-v04-c09-p0040), [v4 c17 P18](../source/v04-c17.md#nw-v04-c17-p0018), [v4 c20 P15](../source/v04-c20.md#nw-v04-c20-p0015), [v4 c24 P40](../source/v04-c24.md#nw-v04-c24-p0040)_

## History

Captain Jim Boyd, born and raised at Four Winds, ran away to sea as a young lad and spent the majority of his life as a sailor, travelling to the far corners of the earth and surviving innumerable perils. In his youth he fell in love with a girl named Margaret, but she tragically vanished at sea during a sudden squall, an event that shaped his emotional life forever as he remained devoted to her memory. Eventually retiring from the sea, he became the keeper of the Four Winds Light at the harbor entrance. When Gilbert and Anne Blythe moved to the shore, Captain Jim immediately befriended them as 'kindred spirits.' He welcomed Owen Ford, the grandson of his old friend the schoolmaster, and collaborated with him by providing his lifelong journal to be written into 'The Life-Book of Captain Jim.' Captain Jim also took a deep interest in Leslie Moore's welfare, having been the one to find her husband in Cuba years prior. After seeing his 'life-book' published and receiving his first printed copy, Captain Jim passed away peacefully in his sleep at the lighthouse, his hands resting on the opened manuscript.

_Sources: [v4 c6 P8](../source/v04-c06.md#nw-v04-c06-p0008), [v4 c6 P14](../source/v04-c06.md#nw-v04-c06-p0014), [v4 c7 P47](../source/v04-c07.md#nw-v04-c07-p0047), [v4 c9 P3](../source/v04-c09.md#nw-v04-c09-p0003), [v4 c9 P36](../source/v04-c09.md#nw-v04-c09-p0036), [v4 c9 P50](../source/v04-c09.md#nw-v04-c09-p0050), [v4 c11 P33](../source/v04-c11.md#nw-v04-c11-p0033), [v4 c20 P12](../source/v04-c20.md#nw-v04-c20-p0012), [v4 c24 P21](../source/v04-c24.md#nw-v04-c24-p0021), [v4 c25 P4](../source/v04-c25.md#nw-v04-c25-p0004), [v4 c39 P5](../source/v04-c39.md#nw-v04-c39-p0005), [v4 c39 P25](../source/v04-c39.md#nw-v04-c39-p0025), [v4 c39 P28](../source/v04-c39.md#nw-v04-c39-p0028)_

## Background by volume

- Ran away to sea as a boy of sixteen  <sub>[v4 c7 P47](../source/v04-c07.md#nw-v04-c07-p0047)</sub>
- Spent a lifetime sailing the globe, experiencing shipwrecks, fires, mutonies, and pirates  <sub>[v4 c9 P36](../source/v04-c09.md#nw-v04-c09-p0036), [v4 c9 P50](../source/v04-c09.md#nw-v04-c09-p0050)</sub>
- Lost his sweetheart, Margaret, when her boat drifted out to sea during a squall fifty years prior  <sub>[v4 c20 P12](../source/v04-c20.md#nw-v04-c20-p0012)</sub>
- Discovered the long-lost, brain-injured George Moore in Havana and brought him back to Four Winds  <sub>[v4 c11 P33](../source/v04-c11.md#nw-v04-c11-p0033), [v4 c13 P15](../source/v04-c13.md#nw-v04-c13-p0015)</sub>

## Quotes

> The race that knows Joseph is the salt of the airth, I reckon.  <sub>[v4 c7 P60](../source/v04-c07.md#nw-v04-c07-p0060)</sub>

> I’ve kind of contracted a habit of enj’ying things. It’s got so chronic that I believe I even enj’y the disagreeable things.  <sub>[v4 c17 P18](../source/v04-c17.md#nw-v04-c17-p0018)</sub>

> If it wasn’t for our dreams they might as well bury us. How’d we stand living if it wasn’t for our dream of immortality?  <sub>[v4 c20 P8](../source/v04-c20.md#nw-v04-c20-p0008)</sub>

> There’s a vast of onunderstandable things in life, ain’t there, Mistress Blythe?  <sub>[v4 c17 P10](../source/v04-c17.md#nw-v04-c17-p0010)</sub>

> I reckon that whatever the New Year brings us will be the best the Great Captain has for us—and somehow or other we’ll all make port in a good harbor.  <sub>[v4 c16 P22](../source/v04-c16.md#nw-v04-c16-p0022)</sub>
